items.statement: When a question asks for a percentage of clients matching a condition, the denominator counts distinct clients rather than joined rows, so the join path must not multiply client rows.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of clients and the schema links clients to accounts through a disposition table.

items.statement: Wrapping a single-row existence check in CASE WHEN EXISTS ... THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END produces a result shape that differs from a direct conditional projection over the joined row.
items.when: The question expects one row per matching card rather than a single aggregate answer.

items.statement: A yes/no question about whether a card's set has a non-null mtgoCode is answered by joining cards to sets on setCode and selecting a conditional on sets.mtgoCode, not by an EXISTS subquery returning a single 'Yes'/'No' literal.
items.when: The question asks whether a named card's set appears on Magic: The Gathering Online and the schema has cards.setCode and sets.mtgoCode.

items.statement: Filtering posts.Title for a value that is stored in postHistory.Text returns no rows and is not a valid way to locate a post by its text.
items.when: The question supplies a post title or body string and the schema stores that string in postHistory.Text.

items.statement: A question that asks for the user who last edited a post joins postHistory to posts on PostId and then to users on the post's LastEditorUserId, filtering postHistory.Text for the post title.
items.when: The question asks for the last editor of a post identified by its title or text rather than by its Id.

items.statement: A query that returns a named attribute for a set of matching rows must use DISTINCT when the question asks for names and the underlying table can contain multiple rows sharing that name.
items.when: The question asks to list names of entities matching a condition and the selected column is not a key of the table.

items.statement: When a date range filter is applied to a column whose values include a time component, the comparison must normalize the column to a date-only value before comparing it to the range bounds.
items.when: The question asks for rows within a date range and the filtered column stores datetime strings rather than plain dates.

items.statement: A question that asks two separate things requires a single SQL statement joining the relevant tables, not multiple statements.
items.when: The question contains more than one interrogative clause whose answers come from different tables.

items.statement: Questions asking for the aim or purpose of a total debited amount are answered from the order table grouped by account_id and k_symbol with SUM(amount), not from individual trans rows.
items.when: The question asks what a summed amount was for, rather than asking for a single transaction matching that amount.

items.statement: When a percentage is requested over posts, the denominator counts all posts in the posts table rather than only posts that join to users.
items.when: the question asks for a percentage of posts and the query joins posts to users

items.statement: A percentage of posts matching a condition is computed as the count of matching posts divided by the total count of posts, not by the count of posts joined to users.
items.when: the question asks for the percentage of posts satisfying a condition on post attributes or owner attributes

items.statement: A school-type filter naming both Intermediate/Middle Schools and Unified Schools is expressed as SOC = 62 AND DOC = 54, not as an OR between the two codes.
items.when: the question names two school types that map to distinct SOC and DOC codes

items.statement: When a question asks for administrator e-mail addresses of schools, the answer returns the AdmEmail1 and AdmEmail2 columns as separate output columns rather than unpivoting them into a single column via UNION.
items.when: the question asks for valid administrator e-mail addresses of schools

items.statement: A query that filters on columns from both joined tables keeps each filter predicate attached to its own table alias.
items.when: The query joins two tables and the question's conditions reference columns from both of them.

items.statement: When a question asks for attributes from more than one table, the SELECT clause lists each requested attribute rather than only one of them.
items.when: The question requests attributes belonging to two different tables joined in the query.

items.statement: Counting clients in a percentage aggregate uses COUNT on the client identifier rather than COUNT(*).
items.when: The aggregate divides a count of clients by a total and the client table is joined to other tables.

items.statement: A percentage of clients filtered by a district attribute is computed by joining client directly to district on district_id, without routing through disp or account.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of clients whose district satisfies a condition on a district column.

items.statement: The order of selected columns follows the order in which the question requests them.
items.when: The question names a measure before naming the identifier to list.

items.statement: A requested percentage that is not stored as a column must be computed from its numerator and denominator columns rather than selected from a similarly named column.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage and the table offers count and enrollment columns but no matching percentage column.

items.statement: A per-post favorite threshold filters individual post rows and does not aggregate favorite counts across a user's posts.
items.when: The question mentions a total or aggregate favorite amount but the filter is applied to a single child column without GROUP BY or HAVING.

items.statement: Counting users joined to a one-to-many child table requires COUNT(DISTINCT parent key) rather than COUNT(parent key) to avoid inflating the count by duplicate join rows.
items.when: The query counts parent rows while joining to a child table that can have multiple rows per parent.

items.statement: Selecting foreign key id columns (eye_colour_id, hair_colour_id, skin_colour_id) instead of joining the colour table and returning colour names does not satisfy a request for colour values.
items.when: The question asks for colour names of superheroes and the schema has a colour table with a colour column.

items.statement: When a question asks for colour values such as eyes, hair, or skin, the answer must select the colour name from the colour table rather than the foreign key id column on the superhero table.
items.when: The question asks for a colour attribute (eye, hair, or skin colour) of superheroes.

items.statement: Existence conditions between two tables are expressed as an INNER JOIN on the shared key when the aggregate is computed over the joined rows.
items.when: The question requires rows from one table to have matching rows in another table and the answer aggregates a column from the first table.

items.statement: A filter on a column of the table being aggregated must be applied in the outer query's WHERE clause, not inside an EXISTS subquery, when the filter does not depend on the correlated subquery's rows.
items.when: The question asks for an aggregate over rows of one table while also requiring existence of related rows in another table.

items.statement: A grade span of Kindergarten to 8th grade is matched against the GSoffered column value 'K-8' rather than against separate Low Grade and High Grade columns.
items.when: The question specifies a grade span such as Kindergarten to 8th grade and the schools table exposes a GSoffered column.

items.statement: A question asking for a count per city is answered with a GROUP BY on the city column and one row per city, not a single aggregate row.
items.when: The question asks for a number of schools for each city or otherwise requests per-city breakdowns.

items.statement: Joining the cards table directly to the set-translations table and applying LIMIT 1 is not equivalent to filtering set-translations by the set code obtained from the card.
items.when: The question asks for a single translated set name for a card identified by name.

items.statement: A query that returns a set's translated name for a card name uses a subquery on the card table to obtain the set code, then filters the set-translations table by that code and the target language.
items.when: The question asks for a set's name in a given language for a card identified by name.

items.statement: Queries that rank heroes by an attribute value join superhero to hero_attribute and attribute, filter attribute_name, and order by hero_attribute.attribute_value descending with LIMIT 1.
items.when: The question asks which superhero has the highest or lowest value of a named attribute.

items.statement: String literal comparisons against attribute_name values are case-sensitive in this schema, so the stored casing (e.g. 'Durability') must match the literal exactly.
items.when: The query filters an attribute or category name column by a string literal.

items.statement: A filter on a column of a joined table references that table's alias rather than the base table name.
items.when: The query joins multiple tables and filters on a column belonging to one of the joined tables.

items.statement: A numeric range stated as exceeding a lower bound and not exceeding an upper bound is expressed with BETWEEN using the lower and upper bounds inclusive.
items.when: The question specifies a value greater than one number and less than or equal to another number.

items.statement: Filtering a boolean-like column with an IN list of literal values is not equivalent to filtering with an equality comparison on that column when the column stores single-character flags.
items.when: The query filters a column whose values are single-character flags such as 'F' or 'T'.

items.statement: When a question asks which group has the most rows and also asks for the amount, the query must return both the group label and the count, ordered by that count descending with a limit of one.
items.when: The question asks for the top group by number of rows and also asks to indicate the amount.

items.statement: When a question asks which entity ranks highest on a numeric attribute, the query orders by that attribute descending and limits to one row while projecting only the entity identifier.
items.when: The question names specific entities and asks which one has the larger value of a numeric column.

items.statement: A comparison question that asks which of several named entities ranks highest on a numeric attribute is answered by selecting only the identifying column, not the compared attribute.
items.when: The question asks which of two or more named rows has the greater or lesser value of a numeric column.

items.statement: A difference between two per-user aggregates is computed in a single query using conditional aggregation (SUM(IIF(condition, value, 0)) for each user) rather than two scalar subqueries subtracted.
items.when: The question asks for the difference between two aggregates each filtered to a different named entity.

items.statement: View counts for a user's posts are obtained by joining users to posts through postHistory (users.Id = postHistory.UserId, postHistory.PostId = posts.Id), not through posts.OwnerUserId.
items.when: The question asks for an aggregate over posts attributed to a named user in the codebase_community schema.

items.statement: A percentage comparison between two entities' ratings is computed from both entities' rating values in the same query, not from one entity's rating joined against the other's row.
items.when: The question asks how much higher one named entity's rating is than another named entity's rating.

items.statement: When a question compares a metric between two named entities, each entity's value must be selected by filtering on that entity's name rather than by joining one entity's row to the other's.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage or difference between a metric of two specifically named entities.

items.statement: A filter on expense.approved is not applied when the question does not mention approval status.
items.when: The question asks for expense totals for an event without referencing approval.

items.statement: When a question asks for the type of expenses, the grouping column is budget.type rather than budget.category.
items.when: The question asks for the type of expenses associated with an event.

items.statement: When a question asks for account holder identification numbers, the result column is the client identifier from the disposition table rather than the account identifier.
items.when: The question names account holders or clients as the requested output while the transaction table only carries account identifiers.

items.statement: A subquery computing an average for comparison must apply the same row filters as the outer query when the question scopes both to the same subset.
items.when: The question asks for rows whose value is below an average and specifies a filter that applies to the population being averaged.

items.statement: A percentage of posts attributed to a user is computed with the user's post count as the denominator, so the denominator must count the same post set that the numerator filters.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of a user's posts meeting a condition.

items.statement: Tag membership for a post is determined by joining tags to postHistory on ExcerptPostId = PostId and postHistory to users on UserId, not by pattern-matching the posts.Tags string.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of posts associated with a named tag or language.

items.statement: When a question asks for a driver's reference name, the answer includes forename and surname alongside driverRef.
items.when: The question asks for a driver's reference name or name.

items.statement: In the formula_1 schema, the results column that records finishing rank is named rank, not positionOrder.
items.when: The question asks for a driver's finishing position or rank in a race.

items.statement: A CASE expression that yields a boolean uses true and false as its result values.
items.when: The answer column is a CASE expression whose branches represent a yes/no outcome.

items.statement: Boolean yes/no questions are answered with a CASE expression returning true and false rather than string labels such as 'Yes' and 'No'.
items.when: The question asks a yes/no question about a row's attributes.

items.statement: Selecting DISTINCT district names with an ORDER BY on the name does not answer a question that asks for the top ten districts by withdrawal amount.
items.when: The question asks for a top-N ranking of districts by a numeric aggregate.

items.statement: A question asking for top-N districts by an aggregate amount requires grouping by district and ordering by the aggregate, not selecting distinct district names.
items.when: The question asks for a ranking of districts by a summed or counted measure.

items.statement: A percentage denominator counts the rows that satisfy the question's filters, so the count is taken over the filtered base table rather than over all rows of a joined table.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of a filtered subset of patients.

items.statement: A filter on a column that exists in the base table belongs in the WHERE clause against that table rather than being pushed through a join to a second table.
items.when: The question filters on a column that is present in the primary table and the query joins another table.

items.statement: Grouping by a molecule-level label together with the grouped column and ordering by COUNT(*) does not rank bond types within a molecule, since each (bond_type, label) pair forms its own group.
items.when: The query groups by both a per-molecule attribute and a per-bond attribute while ranking by an aggregate count.

items.statement: When a question asks for a single attribute of a grouped aggregate (such as the bond type with the highest count) alongside a separate molecule-level attribute, the aggregate must be computed in a subquery and the molecule-level attribute joined or selected separately, because grouping by both the aggregate key and the molecule attribute collapses the aggregate to one row per group.
items.when: The question asks for the top group by count within a molecule and also asks for a molecule-level property such as a carcinogenicity label.

items.statement: Joining posts to users through a post-history table rather than the post ownership column changes which posts are attributed to each user and can alter the comparison result.
items.when: The schema contains both a direct post-to-user ownership column and a separate post-history table linking users to posts.

items.statement: When a question compares popularity across users, the popularity measure must be aggregated over the posts each user authored, joined through the post-to-user ownership relationship.
items.when: The question asks which of several named users has higher popularity and the schema links posts to users by an owner column.

items.statement: A query returning a single attribute from a join that can match multiple rows must use SELECT DISTINCT to avoid duplicate values.
items.when: The question asks for one attribute and the joins may produce multiple matching rows per entity.

items.statement: String literals compared against a categorical column must match the stored value's casing, such as 'Human' rather than 'human'.
items.when: The query filters a text column by an equality condition on a category value.

items.statement: A driver's first race is identified by ordering races by year ascending and taking the earliest, without requiring a round tiebreaker.
items.when: The question asks for a driver's first race event.

items.statement: Points recorded for a driver's race event are stored in driverStandings, not in results.
items.when: The question asks for a driver's points at a specific race.

items.statement: A subquery that selects DISTINCT CustomerIDs from transactions and joins back to yearmonth is not equivalent to a direct join when the question only requires the consumption value, because the direct join preserves the same filtering without the extra projection.
items.when: The question asks only for a consumption value and the customer filter is expressed entirely in the transactions table.

items.statement: When a question asks for a consumption status for a given month, the yearmonth row is joined to qualifying transactions on CustomerID and filtered by the month's Date value.
items.when: The question asks for a consumption value from the yearmonth table for a specific month for customers selected by transaction conditions.

items.statement: Counting accounts with running contracts uses COUNT on account_id without DISTINCT because each account is counted once per qualifying loan join.
items.when: The question asks how many accounts have running contracts and the query joins account to loan.

items.statement: A loan status of 'D' represents a running contract alongside status 'C', so counting running contracts requires filtering on both statuses.
items.when: The question asks for accounts with running contracts and the loan table has a status column.

items.statement: Joining a table that is not needed to satisfy the question's filters or aggregates introduces execution mismatches.
items.when: The question's filters and aggregates reference columns all available in one table.

items.statement: A ratio between two counts of schools filtered by a single categorical column is computed from one table without joining unrelated tables.
items.when: The question asks for a ratio of two subsets of the same entity distinguished only by a categorical column value.

items.statement: Table aliases (T1, T2) and explicit INNER JOIN syntax are used in the corrected query form.
items.when: The query involves joining two tables on a foreign key relationship.

items.statement: Queries that join a child table to a parent table and select columns from both can return duplicate rows when the child table has multiple rows per parent, so DISTINCT is needed to match the expected result set.
items.when: The question asks for a parent-level attribute alongside child-level attributes and the child table may contain multiple rows per parent key.

items.statement: A foreign name for a card is retrieved from foreign_data.name, joined to cards on uuid, with the language filter applied to foreign_data.language.
items.when: The question asks for a card's foreign name in a specific language.

items.statement: The cards table stores the card type in a column named types, not type.
items.when: The question filters cards by card type.

items.statement: Ordering results.fastestLap to find a driver's fastest lap yields a different race than ordering lapTimes.milliseconds, because results.fastestLap records a per-result lap rank rather than a lap time.
items.when: The question asks for the race of a driver's fastest lap and the schema contains both results.fastestLap and lapTimes.milliseconds.

items.statement: A question asking for the race in which a driver had his fastest lap is answered from lapTimes joined to races and drivers, ordering by lapTimes.milliseconds, not from results.fastestLap.
items.when: The question asks for the race and year of a driver's fastest lap.

items.statement: The phrase 'would remain in his position when the team attacked' maps to the attacking_work_rate column with value 'low'.
items.when: The question describes a player's tendency to stay in position during team attacks.

items.statement: Counting rows that satisfy a set of equality filters on a single table uses COUNT(column) rather than COUNT(DISTINCT column) when the filtered column set does not include a key that could repeat.
items.when: The question asks how many rows match one or more equality conditions on a single table and no join or grouping is involved.

items.statement: An average price per item is computed as the sum of per-row price-to-amount ratios, not as the ratio of summed prices to summed amounts.
items.when: The question asks for an average price per single item and the detail table stores price and amount as separate columns per row.

items.statement: When a question asks for the top entity by a metric that is stored in a separate aggregate table, the ranking must be computed from that table rather than from the detail rows.
items.when: The question asks for a top-ranked entity by a total or consumption metric and the schema contains a pre-aggregated table holding that metric per entity.

items.statement: Grouping by the entity key and applying HAVING on a joined row count produces per-entity rows instead of a single aggregate over the qualifying entities.
items.when: The question asks for an aggregate value over a set of entities selected by a threshold on their related-row count.

items.statement: A query that filters users by an aggregate over their posts must aggregate posts in a subquery before joining to users, so the outer aggregate is computed over the filtered user set rather than per user.
items.when: The question asks for an average or other aggregate over users who satisfy a condition on the count of their related posts.

items.statement: Counting cards that match a condition on ruling text requires joining cards to rulings on uuid and counting distinct card ids.
items.when: The question counts cards whose matching text lives in the rulings table.

items.statement: Text about a card's abilities is stored in the rulings table, not in the cards table.
items.when: The question asks for cards whose text mentions an ability or ruling detail.

items.statement: A percentage computed as a ratio of counts must use CAST(... AS REAL) or an equivalent float conversion so integer division does not truncate the result.
items.when: The answer is a percentage or ratio derived from COUNT expressions over integer columns.

items.statement: Questions asking for a driver's finishing-position percentage over a season range are answered from driverStandings joined to races and drivers, not from the results table.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of a driver's race outcomes (such as not finishing first) since a given year.

items.statement: Joining Patient and Examination tables is unnecessary when the requested output columns and all filter conditions are satisfied by the Laboratory table alone.
items.when: The question asks only for patient IDs and all predicates reference columns present in the Laboratory table.

items.statement: A date range that qualifies a laboratory measurement is applied to the laboratory record's own date column, not to an examination date column from a joined table.
items.when: The question constrains a lab value (such as GPT or ALB) together with a date range and the schema has a date column on the laboratory table.

items.statement: Joins that connect an event to a member through budget and expense tables are ordered event -> budget -> expense -> member, following the foreign keys link_to_event, link_to_budget, and link_to_member.
items.when: The question names an event and asks for a member associated with it through budget and expense records.

items.statement: A query that returns a person's name from a chain of foreign-key joins must not include a LIMIT clause, because the LIMIT can truncate the result to fewer rows than the join produces.
items.when: The question asks which person is associated with a named entity and the answer is reached through a multi-table join.

items.statement: Joining yearmonth twice on CustomerID with Date equal to a bare year string does not match the yearmonth Date values, which are stored as full dates.
items.when: The query needs per-year consumption from the yearmonth table and the Date column holds full date values rather than year labels.

items.statement: A customer identified by a transaction attribute is located through a subquery on transactions_1k, and the yearmonth rows for that customer are then aggregated with conditional sums per year.
items.when: The question identifies a customer by a transaction attribute (such as a price paid on a date) and asks for a rate comparing two years of consumption.

items.statement: Joining schools to satscores uses schools.CDSCode = satscores.cds, and the table holding the ranking column is the one whose column is ordered.
items.when: The question involves school telephone numbers together with SAT average scores.

items.statement: When a query orders by a nullable column and takes the top row, rows with NULL in that column must be excluded so the result reflects the lowest non-null value.
items.when: The question asks for the row with the minimum or maximum value of a column that may contain NULLs.

items.statement: A NOT NULL filter is applied to every selected column that can be null, not only to one of them.
items.when: The query selects multiple columns and the question implies excluding rows with missing values.

items.statement: When a question asks for multiple distinct attributes of the same entity, each requested attribute is selected as its own column rather than combined into a single column.
items.when: The question names more than one attribute to list for the same entity.

items.statement: When a question asks for a percentage of entities matching a condition, the denominator must count only entities matching that condition rather than all entities in the table.
items.when: The question requests a percentage of a described subset of rows.

items.statement: A percentage computed over a filtered subset must divide by the count of that same filtered subset, not by the total row count of the base table.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of rows satisfying a condition while also reporting a count of a narrower subset.

items.statement: Comparing aggregates across two groups is expressed as one aggregate query per group combined with UNION, then ordered by the aggregate with LIMIT 1 to select the winning group label.
items.when: The question asks which of two groups has the higher or lower average of a column.

items.statement: When a question asks which of two groups has the higher average of a metric, the answer is the group label, not a member row of that group.
items.when: The question compares an aggregate metric between two named groups and asks which group wins.

items.statement: In the loan table, status value 'C' denotes an account that is still running with no issue.
items.when: the question refers to accounts that are still running, current, or without issue and the loan table has a status column

items.statement: A percentage of accounts is computed as a count of qualifying accounts divided by a count of all accounts, not as a sum of amounts divided by a sum of amounts.
items.when: the question asks for a percentage of accounts or rows rather than a percentage of a monetary or quantity total

items.statement: When a filter condition applies to a column of one table but the counted entity is identified in another table, the condition belongs in a conditional aggregate over the entity's identifier rather than in a WHERE clause that removes rows.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of entities satisfying a condition and the condition's column is in a table other than the one holding the entity identifier.

items.statement: A percentage of molecules matching a condition must divide the count of distinct molecule identifiers meeting the condition by the count of distinct molecule identifiers in the relevant population, not by a row count of a joined table.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of molecules and the query joins a molecule table to a table with multiple rows per molecule.

items.statement: Grouping by a post identifier alongside post title and comment text is unnecessary when the title and comment text already uniquely determine the grouping rows.
items.when: The query groups by a post's title and comment text and also includes the post identifier in the GROUP BY clause.

items.statement: A tag filter on a delimited Tags column matches the exact tag value rather than a substring pattern when the requested tag is a single complete tag.
items.when: The question names one specific tag and the Tags column stores tags in a delimited format.

items.statement: When a question asks for the complete address of a school identified by a satscores metric, the satscores table is joined to schools on cds = CDSCode and the address columns are selected from schools.
items.when: The question names address fields (Street, City, Zip, State) together with a satscores-derived ranking.

items.statement: A lowest-ratio query over satscores must not filter out rows where NumTstTakr is zero or null, because the ratio is undefined there and excluding them changes which school is selected.
items.when: The question asks for the school with the lowest excellence rate computed as NumGE1500 divided by NumTstTakr.

items.statement: Using NOT EXISTS over an atom subquery to express absence of an element yields a different result than counting distinct molecules whose joined atom rows all have a non-matching element.
items.when: The question asks for molecules that do not contain a particular atom element and the schema links molecules to atoms by molecule_id.

items.statement: A percentage of molecules that lack a given atom element is computed as the count of distinct molecules with no matching atom row divided by the count of distinct molecules in the target label group, not by a subquery over the molecule table alone.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of molecules that do not contain a specified atom element.

items.statement: When a question asks to list entities by their ID alongside an aggregate, the IDs are returned as a separate column rather than omitted.
items.when: The question requests both a numeric aggregate and a listing of the matching rows' identifiers.

items.statement: A percentage requested over a filtered subset of rows is computed with the filter applied to both the numerator and the denominator, not to the numerator alone over the full table count.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of rows satisfying a condition and the answer is compared against a value derived from the filtered subset.

items.statement: A query answering a question about a user's action on a post must select the post's title column in addition to the user's display name.
items.when: The question references a post by its title and asks which user acted on it.

items.statement: When a question asks which user performed an action on a post, the result must include both the user's display name and the post's title.
items.when: The question asks which user added a bounty to a post identified by its title.

items.statement: When a question asks for a value at the time of an examination, the date column used for age computation must come from the examination or laboratory record joined on patient ID, not from a separate examination table joined only on ID and date.
items.when: The question asks for an age or duration computed from a date that belongs to a laboratory or examination event.

items.statement: A query that asks for the row with the maximum value of a column must order by that column descending and limit to one row, rather than filtering with a subquery that compares against MAX of the column.
items.when: The question asks for the patient or record having the highest or lowest value of a numeric column.

items.statement: Division of two integer-typed columns is cast to a real type on the numerator to produce a fractional rate.
items.when: The query computes a ratio between two count or enrollment columns.

items.statement: A numeric column compared to a literal value is compared using the literal's numeric type rather than as a quoted string.
items.when: The query filters a column whose values are numeric codes against a constant.

items.statement: Per-category counts are computed with COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN <category condition> THEN <id> ELSE NULL END) aliased per category.
items.when: The question requests distinct counts broken out by a categorical column value.

items.statement: A question asking for separate counts of two categories requires one count expression per category rather than a single combined count.
items.when: The question asks how many items exist for each of two or more named categories.

items.statement: Selecting postHistory columns as the result does not answer a question that asks for comments.
items.when: The question's requested output is comments and the query's select list draws from postHistory.

items.statement: A question asking for comments left by users who edited a post requires joining comments to postHistory on the editing user's id, not selecting postHistory rows as the output.
items.when: The question asks for comments authored by users who edited a specific post.

items.statement: A count of patients satisfying a join condition uses COUNT on the patient identifier without DISTINCT when the join key is the patient identifier and each patient row is unique.
items.when: The question asks how many patients match a condition and the query joins Patient to another table on the patient ID.

items.statement: Age at the time of an event is computed as the difference between the event year and the birth year, not by comparing the birth year alone to an age threshold.
items.when: The question asks for a count of patients or people filtered by an age condition relative to a dated event.

items.statement: A query that returns a user attribute for the owner of a post joins posts to users on posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id.
items.when: The question asks for an attribute of the user who owns a post.

items.statement: String literals compared against a text column must match the value in the question exactly, including trailing punctuation such as a question mark.
items.when: The question quotes a literal value to filter on and that value ends with punctuation.

items.statement: A completion rate over drivers in a race counts only rows whose time value is non-null in the numerator while the denominator counts all participating drivers.
items.when: The question asks for a race completion rate for drivers who took part in a specific race.

items.statement: A rate expressed as a percentage is computed by multiplying the ratio by 100.
items.when: The question asks for a rate or proportion and the expected answer is on a 0-100 scale rather than a 0-1 fraction.

items.statement: A comparison against an aggregate over a filtered subset requires the same filter to be applied inside the aggregate subquery.
items.when: The question asks for rows whose value exceeds an average computed over a filtered subset of the same rows.

items.statement: The DOC column in the schools table holds the school's DOC type.
items.when: The question asks for the DOC type of schools.

items.statement: A query that returns an age computed from two date columns must also return the underlying birth date column so the computed age is verifiable.
items.when: The question asks for a patient's age at an event and the age is derived by subtracting year parts of two date columns.

items.statement: When ordering rows to find an extreme (oldest/youngest) by a nullable date column, rows with NULL in that column must be excluded so they do not sort first or last incorrectly.
items.when: The query orders by a date column that may contain NULL values to select an extreme row.

items.statement: A column referenced in the SELECT list must exist on a table that is joined in the query, and the join path must reach the table that owns the requested attribute.
items.when: The question asks for an attribute that is not stored on the table filtered by the WHERE clause.

items.statement: A date literal compared against a date column must use the column's stored format, including zero-padded month and day components.
items.when: The query filters on a date column using a literal date value.

items.statement: When a question asks for the segments with the biggest and lowest percentage increases, the result is one row containing both the top and bottom segment and their percentages, not a ranked list of all segments.
items.when: the question asks for both the biggest and lowest values of a metric across a small fixed set of categories

items.statement: Percentage change between two years is computed as (later − earlier) / earlier × 100, dividing by the earlier year's value.
items.when: the question asks for a percentage increase or decrease between two periods

items.statement: Year comparisons on date columns are expressed by extracting the year with strftime('%Y', column) and comparing to a year string, rather than comparing the full date to a date literal.
items.when: The question specifies a year threshold (e.g., opened after 1991, closed before 2000) against a date or datetime column.

items.statement: When a question asks for a column that may be absent for some matching rows, the join to the table supplying that column must be a LEFT JOIN so rows without a match are still returned.
items.when: The question asks to list a column from a table that is not guaranteed to have a matching row for every qualifying row in the primary table.

items.statement: Casting a numeric column to REAL before ORDER BY DESC is unnecessary when the column already stores numeric values, since the cast does not change the ordering outcome.
items.when: The query orders by a column descending to find a maximum and the column's declared type is already numeric.

items.statement: Filtering out NULL values in a column that is used for ORDER BY DESC is unnecessary, because NULLs sort last in descending order in SQLite and do not affect which non-NULL maximum is selected.
items.when: The question asks for the row with the maximum value of a column that may contain NULLs, and the query orders by that column descending with a LIMIT 1.

items.statement: When a question asks for the least-consuming customers within each segment, the minimum consumption must be computed per segment (grouped by segment) rather than as a single global minimum.
items.when: The question mentions a per-segment or per-group least/minimum consumption and the answer must be comparable across segments.

items.statement: Filtering yearmonth rows to those whose Consumption equals the global minimum Consumption across all rows restricts the aggregation to a single customer rather than to the least-consuming customers within each segment.
items.when: The question asks for an average over customers with the least consumption per segment or per group, and the query applies a MIN subquery on the consumption column without correlating it to the group.

items.statement: A condition on school level (such as high school) is expressed through the School Type column rather than through grade-span text in GSoffered.
items.when: The question restricts results to a school level such as high school.

items.statement: A filter on a city name matches the City column, while a filter on a county name matches the County column.
items.when: The question names a geographic place that could be either a city or a county.

items.statement: Joining connected to bond on bond_id does not reflect the schema's relationship between those tables.
items.when: The query joins the connected and bond tables.

items.statement: Joining atom to bond requires the molecule_id column, while joining atom to connected requires the atom_id column.
items.when: The query must relate atoms to bonds and to the connected table.

items.statement: A filter stated in the question (such as a promotional-printing flag) must appear as a predicate in the query, not only as a selected column.
items.when: The question mentions a condition on a column value in addition to asking for that column to be reported.

items.statement: When a question asks for the entity with the most related rows, the ranking must be computed per entity (e.g., by grouping on the entity's key and counting its related rows), not by counting rows across a join that can multiply the entity's rows.
items.when: The question asks for the item with the most of some related record and the answer requires joining a one-to-many table.

items.statement: A query that ranks groups by an aggregate uses GROUP BY on the grouping column and a window function such as RANK() OVER (ORDER BY aggregate DESC) to produce the rank column.
items.when: The requested output includes a rank or ordering of groups by a count or other aggregate.

items.statement: When a question asks to rank groups by an aggregate, the result rows are one per group with the aggregate and a rank computed over that aggregate, not one row per underlying entity.
items.when: The question asks to rank categories or groups by how common or popular they are.

items.statement: A query that asks who is the youngest among drivers who finished a race filters results to rows where the finish time is not null.
items.when: The question restricts the driver set to those who finished the race.

items.statement: A query that asks who is the youngest among a set of drivers selects only the identifying name columns, not the birth-date column used for ordering.
items.when: The question asks for the identity of the youngest or oldest driver and the answer is expected to be a name.

items.statement: When a question asks for a player's age, the player's name column is not required in the result unless the question explicitly asks for names.
items.when: The question asks only for age and does not mention player names.

items.statement: A question asking for a player's current age requires computing the difference between the current date and the player's birthday, not merely the difference between the current year and the birth year.
items.when: The question asks for a player's age at present.

items.statement: A question asking for a peak month returns a month value, not a full date string.
items.when: The question asks for a month as the answer.

items.statement: When a question asks for a peak month within a year, the month is extracted from the date column and rows are grouped by that month with consumption summed before ordering and limiting.
items.when: The question asks for a peak or maximum month within a year and the date column stores year and month as a string.

items.statement: When a question asks for the youngest client, the client selection must be expressed as an ordering on birth_date with a limit, not as an equality against MAX(birth_date).
items.when: The question asks for the youngest client or clients.

items.statement: A query that must return the accounts of the youngest clients cannot satisfy the youngest-client condition by comparing birth_date to MAX(birth_date) while also filtering on an unrelated district aggregate.
items.when: The question asks for accounts of clients who are youngest and also mentions a second, unrelated aggregate condition.

items.statement: A city or district filter on a name column is expressed with a LIKE pattern (e.g., 'Riverside%') when the column stores district or city names that may carry suffixes.
items.when: The question names a city or district and the filter column is a name column rather than a code column.

items.statement: When a question asks for the average of a per-row score column across grouped rows, the aggregate must be computed with AVG (or SUM/COUNT) over the grouped rows rather than by filtering individual rows on the score threshold.
items.when: The question asks for an average of a score column and imposes a threshold on that average.

items.statement: Date equality filters on event_date are written as a LIKE pattern with a trailing wildcard when the stored value may include a time component.
items.when: The filter compares an event_date column to a literal date and the column may store datetime values.

items.statement: A question asking whether each expense was approved requires only the approval column in the result, not identifying columns such as expense_id or expense_description.
items.when: The question asks whether each expense was approved rather than asking to list or identify the expenses.

items.statement: When a question asks for the oldest female client's district, the district is selected by filtering clients on gender = 'F' and ordering by birth_date ascending with LIMIT 1, rather than ordering the joined result rows by birth_date.
items.when: The question asks for a single oldest female client and a value tied to that client's district.

items.statement: When a question asks for the gap between a selected row's average salary and the maximum average salary, the gap is computed as the maximum district A11 minus the selected district's A11, not as the range MAX(A11) - MIN(A11).
items.when: The question asks for a difference between the selected district's average salary and the highest average salary.

items.statement: Questions asking for a count or attribute of a post identified by a comment's author and timestamp require joining comments to posts on PostId = Id and filtering on the comment's UserId and CreationDate.
items.when: The question names a user, a comment timestamp, and asks for a property of the post that comment was attached to.

items.statement: Date-time literals in SQLite comparisons must use the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' rather than slash-separated dates.
items.when: The query filters a column containing date-time values against a literal date.

items.statement: Questions asking who achieved something return driver identity columns (forename, surname, url) rather than only the url column.
items.when: The question asks who performed an action and also requests an associated attribute such as a website.

items.statement: Lap time values in the formula_1 database are stored without a leading zero before the minutes component, so a time written as 0:01:27 in a question matches a stored value of 1:27.
items.when: The question specifies a lap time with a leading zero in the minutes field and the answer must match the lapTimes.time column.

items.statement: A ratio of two integer counts requires at least one operand to be cast to a floating-point type so the division does not truncate to an integer.
items.when: The SQL expression divides one SUM of integer-valued CASE expressions by another.

items.statement: When a question asks for the ratio of A to B, the numerator must count A and the denominator must count B, in that order.
items.when: The question asks for a ratio of one named group to another named group.

items.statement: Counting rows of a table that is joined one-to-one on its primary key does not require DISTINCT to avoid duplicates.
items.when: The counted entity's table is joined to another table on that table's unique key, so each row appears at most once.

items.statement: String literals compared against a column must match the stored value's casing, so a region value stored as 'north Bohemia' is not matched by 'North Bohemia'.
items.when: The query filters a text column with a literal value whose casing differs from the stored data.

items.statement: When a question asks for an average per molecule, the denominator must be the number of molecules in scope, not the number of atoms or bonds.
items.when: The question asks for an average per molecule and the query joins atom or bond tables.

items.statement: A question asking for an average per molecule requires computing a per-molecule aggregate in a subquery and then averaging those per-molecule values, rather than dividing a total count by a count of atoms or rows.
items.when: The question asks for an average of some quantity per molecule.

items.statement: The cards table column holding the card type is named type, not types.
items.when: The question refers to a card's type or types and the query filters on the cards table.

items.statement: A query that returns a status column from a joined table must use SELECT DISTINCT when multiple rows in the joined table can match a single row in the driving table.
items.when: The question asks for a status or attribute from a table joined on a key that is not unique per driving-table row.

items.statement: A query answering a superlative question returns only the columns the question asks for, not the ordering column used to determine the superlative.
items.when: The question asks who is the oldest or youngest and does not request the date value itself.

items.statement: A query that returns the oldest or youngest entity by a date column must exclude rows where that date column is NULL.
items.when: The question asks for the oldest or youngest record ordered by a nullable date column.

items.statement: A win condition is expressed as a positive goal difference (goals_for minus goals_against > 0) rather than as a direct comparison of the two goal columns.
items.when: The query filters matches to those won by a side and the match table exposes separate goals-for and goals-against columns.

items.statement: A team's win count is grouped by its identifier rather than by its display name when the query aggregates match outcomes per team.
items.when: The query counts wins or other match outcomes per team and joins a team table to a match table.

items.statement: Counting a subset that satisfies an extra attribute condition is expressed as a set difference between the threshold-qualified set and the attribute-excluded set, or equivalently as a filtered count over the threshold-qualified set.
items.when: The question asks how many items meeting a related-table threshold also satisfy a categorical attribute.

items.statement: A question asking how many of a filtered subset satisfy an additional attribute condition requires the attribute filter to be applied after the subset is identified, not inside the subset-defining aggregation.
items.when: The question asks for a count of items that both meet a threshold on a related table and belong to a named category.

items.statement: Counting rows of a table that is joined one-to-one on a primary key does not require DISTINCT to avoid double counting.
items.when: The counted entity's table is joined to another table on that table's primary key, so each row matches at most one partner row.

items.statement: String literals compared against a column must match the stored value's case exactly, since equality comparisons are case-sensitive in the target engine.
items.when: The query filters a text column by an equality predicate on a literal value.

items.statement: A request to list multiple drivers from a qualifying session requires an ORDER BY with LIMIT rather than an equality comparison to a single aggregate value.
items.when: The question asks for a list of drivers rather than a single driver.

items.statement: Questions asking for drivers eliminated in the first qualifying period require selecting the slowest drivers by q1 time, not the fastest.
items.when: The question asks for drivers eliminated in a qualifying period.

items.statement: A year filter on a YYYYMM-encoded date column is expressed by matching the first four characters of the date to the year string.
items.when: The date column stores values in YYYYMM format and the question restricts results to a single calendar year.

items.statement: When a question asks for a customer ranked by total consumption over a year, consumption must be aggregated per customer with SUM before ordering, not taken from a single month row.
items.when: The question asks for a customer with the least or most consumption over a year rather than for a specific month.

items.statement: Wrapping a patient count in COUNT(DISTINCT ...) is unnecessary when the join keys guarantee one row per patient.
items.when: the query counts patients joined to tables keyed on patient ID

items.statement: Counting patients that satisfy a condition across joined tables uses COUNT on the patient ID without DISTINCT when each patient appears at most once per joined row set.
items.when: the question asks how many patients meet a condition and the joins do not multiply patient rows

items.statement: In the thrombosis_prediction Laboratory table, a normal anti-SSB result is stored as 'negative' or '0', not as '-' or '+-'.
items.when: The question asks for patients with a normal level of anti-SSB and the query filters the Laboratory table on that column.

items.statement: In the thrombosis_prediction Laboratory table, a normal anti-centromere result is stored as 'negative' or '0', not as '-' or '+-'.
items.when: The question asks for patients with a normal level of anti-centromere (CENTROMEA) and the query filters the Laboratory table on that column.

items.statement: A filter on a column of a joined table requires that table to be joined in the FROM clause rather than referenced only in a correlated subquery.
items.when: The question's filter condition names a column from a table that is not otherwise joined in the query.

items.statement: A condition that a patient has no symptom is expressed as Symptoms IS NULL on the Examination row, not as the absence of any Examination row with a non-null Symptoms.
items.when: The question asks for patients without symptoms and the Examination table stores symptoms per patient row.

items.statement: When a question asks to find records meeting a condition, the condition must appear as a projected column in the SELECT clause rather than only in the join or WHERE clause.
items.when: The question asks to find or flag records satisfying a condition.

items.statement: A question that asks to list entities and also find matching related records requires an inner join on the related table so that only entities with a matching related record are returned.
items.when: The question asks to list items and additionally find related records that satisfy a condition.

items.statement: Counting patients who satisfy a condition on an examination attribute requires joining the examination table and counting its rows, since the patient table alone does not carry that attribute.
items.when: The question asks how many patients have a property recorded in a table other than the patient table.

items.statement: A filter on a laboratory value that is described as normal matches only the literal values that the schema treats as normal, not every non-positive or ambiguous variant.
items.when: The question constrains a laboratory measurement by a qualitative label such as normal, and the column stores several distinct string encodings.

items.statement: Absence of a related record is expressed with NOT EXISTS over the related table correlated on the shared key, while presence is expressed with a separate EXISTS or join.
items.when: The question asks for entities that have one related record of a given kind but do not have another.

items.statement: A single row in a translation table has one language value, so a predicate combining language = 'Korean' AND language NOT LIKE '%Japanese%' on the same row can never be satisfied.
items.when: The question requires a set to have one translation language and lack another, and translations are stored one language per row.

items.statement: Combining OR and AND predicates without parentheses changes the effective filter because AND binds tighter than OR.
items.when: A WHERE clause mixes an OR over one column with an AND over another column.

items.statement: A filter on a laboratory result column must use the literal values that the column actually stores, not symbolic or abbreviated equivalents.
items.when: The question asks for patients whose lab measurement equals a named qualitative level and the schema stores that level as a coded string.

items.statement: A question asking for the shortest lap time per driver requires grouping by driver and aggregating with MIN over the converted time value.
items.when: The question asks which driver set the shortest lap time and the answer is expected to be one row per driver.

items.statement: Lap times stored as strings in 'M:SS.mmm' format must be converted to a single numeric unit before comparison or ordering.
items.when: The question asks for shortest, fastest, or ordered lap times and the lap time column is a text value containing a colon separator.

items.statement: Table aliases in generated SQL are consistently named T1, T2, and so on in join order, with each column reference qualified by its alias.
items.when: The generated query joins two or more tables and the answer must be executable without ambiguity.

items.statement: Queries that select a non-aggregated column alongside another non-aggregated column from a joined table require a GROUP BY clause listing both selected columns to satisfy strict SQL execution modes.
items.when: The query selects multiple non-aggregated columns from joined tables and the target engine enforces ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY or equivalent.

items.statement: A patient's laboratory attributes are joined to the patient on the shared ID column, and the patient's own attributes are filtered on the patient table.
items.when: The question asks about patients whose laboratory measurement meets a condition and whose patient-level attribute meets another condition.

items.statement: Counting rows that satisfy a filter over a joined table uses COUNT on the primary key column without DISTINCT when the join key is the primary key of the counted table.
items.when: The question asks for a count of entities from one table filtered by a condition on a joined table, and the join is on that table's primary key.

items.statement: Joining drivers to races through driverStandings does not yield the race a driver first joined, because driverStandings records standings entries rather than race participation.
items.when: The question asks for the first race a driver joined and the schema offers both results and driverStandings as paths from drivers to races.

items.statement: A driver's first race is the race with the earliest date among the races in which that driver appears in the results table.
items.when: The question asks for the first race a driver joined and the schema links drivers to races through the results table.

items.statement: A request for a racer's full name is satisfied by selecting the forename and surname columns rather than concatenating them into a single alias.
items.when: The question asks for the full name of a driver.

items.statement: Lap-time columns such as q3 are stored as strings in 'M:SS.mmm' format, so ordering them lexicographically does not produce chronological order.
items.when: The query orders or compares a qualifying time column whose values contain a colon.

items.statement: A numeric range described as between two bounds is implemented with an inclusive BETWEEN predicate.
items.when: The question describes a value as falling within a stated range of bounds.

items.statement: A date filter expressed as 'after <date>' is implemented with a strict comparison that excludes the boundary date.
items.when: The question specifies a date with 'after' rather than 'on or after'.

items.statement: Atom identifiers encode the atom position as the final character, so selecting the nth atom uses a suffix comparison on atom_id rather than a fixed-offset substring.
items.when: The question references an ordinal atom position and the atom_id column encodes that position at the end of the string.

items.statement: A question asking for the element of a specific atom position in each qualifying molecule requires DISTINCT element values, not a grouped count of atoms.
items.when: The question asks to list or tally an attribute of a particular atom position within each qualifying parent record rather than to count occurrences.

items.statement: A query that returns an aggregate alongside identifying columns must include those identifying columns in the GROUP BY clause.
items.when: The SELECT list mixes an aggregate function with non-aggregated columns.

items.statement: When a query aggregates points per constructor, grouping by constructor name alone is sufficient because constructor names are unique in the constructors table.
items.when: The query aggregates constructorResults points and joins constructors, and the answer must identify a single constructor.

items.statement: A normal IgG range stated as strictly between two bounds is expressed with BETWEEN, which includes both endpoints.
items.when: The question describes a laboratory value as normal or within a stated range with two numeric bounds.

items.statement: A count of patients that joins Patient to both Laboratory and Examination must count Patient.ID rather than a column from a joined table, because the join can multiply rows per patient.
items.when: The query counts patients and joins Patient to one or more one-to-many tables such as Laboratory or Examination.

items.statement: A percentage answer is expressed on a 0-100 scale by multiplying the ratio by 100.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage rather than a fraction.

items.statement: A percentage of atoms of a given element among a filtered set of molecules is computed as the count of matching atoms divided by the count of all atoms in those molecules, not by the count of distinct molecules.
items.when: The question asks for the percentage of a specific element within a set of molecules.

items.statement: Joining Player to Player_Attributes is unnecessary when the requested identifier and all filter and sort columns are already present in Player_Attributes.
items.when: The selected column and every WHERE and ORDER BY column belong to Player_Attributes.

items.statement: When a question asks only for player IDs filtered and ordered by attributes that live in Player_Attributes, the query reads those IDs directly from Player_Attributes rather than joining Player.
items.when: The question asks for player IDs and every filter and ordering column it names exists in Player_Attributes.

items.statement: A query that joins a per-card text table to cards and filters by set name can return duplicate rows when a card has multiple matching entries, so DISTINCT is required to return each text once.
items.when: The question asks to list text values for all cards in a set and the joined text table may contain multiple rows per card.

items.statement: Ruling text in a requested language is stored in the foreign_data table, joined to cards on uuid, not in a set_translations table joined on setCode.
items.when: The question asks for card ruling text in a specific non-default language.

items.statement: Joins between a fact table and a lookup table use table aliases, with the lookup table's key column selected when the question asks for the lookup's descriptive attribute.
items.when: The question requests a descriptive attribute that lives in a joined lookup table rather than the filtered entity table.

items.statement: A query that asks for a single attribute of entities named in a filter returns only that attribute, not the filter column alongside it.
items.when: The question asks for one property (such as a publisher) of entities identified by name in a WHERE/IN filter.

items.statement: A finish time value is filtered to the format of a race time (minutes:seconds.milliseconds) when the question asks for a finish time.
items.when: The question asks for a finish time and the results table stores times as strings.

items.statement: A race named in a question is matched against the races table's name column rather than against the circuit hosting it.
items.when: The question names a Grand Prix by event name and the schema has both a races.name column and a circuits table.

items.statement: A condition that defines the population being measured belongs in the WHERE clause, while a condition that defines the numerator subgroup belongs inside the aggregate's CASE expression.
items.when: The question combines a population-level filter with a subgroup whose share is being computed.

items.statement: A percentage of a subgroup within a filtered population uses the subgroup condition in the numerator and the population filter (not the subgroup filter) in the denominator.
items.when: The question asks for the percentage of a subgroup among rows that satisfy a separate filter condition.

items.statement: Counting atoms that satisfy a condition requires counting the atom identifier rather than summing a 1/0 flag when the result is divided by a total atom count.
items.when: The query computes a ratio of matching atoms to all atoms in a filtered set.

items.statement: A percentage composition answer is expressed as a value scaled to 100, not as a fraction between 0 and 1.
items.when: The question asks for a composition or share expressed as a percentage.

items.statement: A year filter on a date column and an age filter on a birth date must both be anchored to the same reference date, namely the examination date, rather than mixing the examination year with the current year.
items.when: The query filters rows by both a calendar year of one date column and an age threshold derived from another date column.

items.statement: Age computed as the difference between the current year and the birth year is not equivalent to age at the time of a historical examination; age must be derived from the examination date and the birth date.
items.when: The question asks for patients below a given age at the time of an examination whose date is fixed in the past.

items.statement: Patient-level questions join Laboratory to Patient on ID rather than querying Laboratory alone.
items.when: the question refers to patients and the answer depends on laboratory measurements

items.statement: Questions asking how one count compares to another require a single scalar difference rather than two separate count columns.
items.when: the question asks how one quantity compares to another quantity

items.statement: A condition on fastest lap time is applied to the results table's fastestLapTime column, not to the drivers table.
items.when: The question mentions fastest lap time and the query joins drivers to results.

items.statement: A driver's birth year is filtered on the drivers table's dob column, not on any column of the results table.
items.when: The question asks for drivers born in a given year and the query joins drivers to results.

items.statement: Counting drivers that satisfy a per-lap condition requires COUNT over the joined driverId without DISTINCT, since a driver may have multiple qualifying laps and the question asks for drivers, not lap rows.
items.when: The question asks how many drivers meet a condition on lapTimes rows.

items.statement: Lap time thresholds expressed in the format mm:ss.ss must be compared against the lapTimes.time column by parsing it into seconds, because lapTimes.milliseconds is not populated in this schema.
items.when: The question specifies a lap time cutoff in a time literal such as 02:00.00 and the query filters lapTimes.

items.statement: A query answering a yes/no question must not include a LIMIT clause that could truncate the result set before the boolean condition is evaluated.
items.when: The question is a yes/no question and the generated SQL contains a LIMIT clause.

items.statement: Yes/no questions whose answer is derived from a boolean column require the query to project a 'YES'/'NO' (or equivalent) literal rather than the raw boolean value.
items.when: The question is phrased as a yes/no question and the answer is determined by a boolean or 0/1 column.

items.statement: Lap-number conditions are evaluated against the laps column of the results table, which is joined to races and drivers, rather than against a separate lap-times table.
items.when: The question filters on lap numbers in the formula_1 schema.

items.statement: A percentage of drivers satisfying a per-lap condition is computed over result rows joined to drivers and races, not over distinct driver identifiers, so the denominator counts qualifying result rows rather than unique drivers.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of drivers and the condition involves a per-lap or per-result attribute such as lap number.

items.statement: A query that filters on a description column must match the stored description value exactly, including its comma-and-space separated list form.
items.when: The question names a set of items that corresponds to a single stored description value.

items.statement: When a question asks for a person's full name, the answer must return the first_name and last_name columns separately rather than concatenating them into a single column.
items.when: The question asks for a full name of a person stored as separate first_name and last_name columns.

items.statement: When a relationship table stores the two endpoints in separate columns, a single join condition must cover both columns to capture all connections.
items.when: The question asks for atoms that cannot bond with any other atoms and the connected table has atom_id and atom_id2 columns.

items.statement: A NOT IN subquery used to find rows with no matching partner must select the join key from the joined table, not the outer table's display column, or the comparison is made against the wrong value set.
items.when: The question asks for entities that cannot bond with any other atoms and the schema has an atom table plus a connected table with two atom-id columns.

items.statement: A join path from comments to users must traverse comments.PostId to posts.Id and posts.OwnerUserId to users.Id when the user is the post owner, not comments.UserId to users.Id.
items.when: The question asks for the display name of the user associated with a post's comments and the schema links users to posts via OwnerUserId.

items.statement: When a question asks for the latest comments, the ordering must use the comment's own creation timestamp rather than a joined user's timestamp.
items.when: The question asks for the most recent comments and the query joins comments to users.

items.statement: A question asking for the date of a player's highest value in an attribute is answered by ordering the attribute descending and taking the earliest date among ties.
items.when: The question asks when a player first achieved their maximum value for some attribute.

items.statement: Joins between Player and Player_Attributes must use player_fifa_api_id, not player_api_id.
items.when: The query joins the Player table to the Player_Attributes table.

items.statement: A client-to-account relationship mediated by a disposition table requires joining on both client_id and account_id to avoid cross-product row inflation.
items.when: The schema contains a disposition-style table linking clients and accounts and the query aggregates over clients.

items.statement: When a question asks for a percentage of clients matching a condition, the denominator counts distinct clients rather than joined rows, so the join path must not multiply client rows.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of clients and the schema links clients to the filtered entity through a many-to-many or multi-hop join path.

items.statement: Wrapping a single-row existence check in CASE WHEN EXISTS ... THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END produces a result shape that differs from a direct conditional projection over the joined row.
items.when: The question expects one row per matching card rather than a single aggregate boolean.

items.statement: A yes/no question about whether a card's set has a non-null mtgoCode is answered by joining cards to sets on setCode and selecting a conditional on sets.mtgoCode, not by an EXISTS subquery returning a single 'Yes'/'No' literal.
items.when: The question asks whether a named card's set appears on Magic: The Gathering Online and the schema has cards.setCode and sets.mtgoCode.

items.statement: Filtering posts.Title for a title string does not locate the postHistory row whose Text matches that title.
items.when: The question's identifying string is a post title and the answer requires a postHistory attribute.

items.statement: A question that asks for the user who last edited a post joins postHistory to posts on PostId and then to users on the post's LastEditorUserId, filtering postHistory.Text for the post title.
items.when: The question asks for the last editor of a post identified by its title rather than by its Id.

items.statement: An aggregate over a nullable time column is filtered with HAVING on the aggregate result when the grouping column can produce groups whose time values are all null.
items.when: The query groups by a column and averages a nullable time column, and some groups may contain no non-null time values.

items.statement: Lap or race times stored as strings in the form H:MM:SS.sss are converted to seconds by parsing the hour, minute, second, and fractional-second components at fixed character offsets rather than by splitting on colons.
items.when: The time column contains values formatted as H:MM:SS.sss and the answer must be an average or sum in seconds.

items.statement: A query that lists names for a category should use DISTINCT when multiple rows can share the same name value.
items.when: The question asks to list names and the underlying table may contain duplicate name values.

items.statement: When a date column stores timestamps with a time component, filtering it against bare date literals requires truncating the column to its date portion first.
items.when: The question asks for rows within a date range and the date column may contain time-of-day components.

items.statement: A yes/no question about a property of a single molecule is answered by selecting that property's column value, not by mapping it through a CASE expression into 'Yes'/'No'.
items.when: The question asks whether a molecule has a property and the property is stored as a categorical label column.

items.statement: Bond type values in the bond table are stored without surrounding spaces, so equality filters on bond_type must use the bare value such as '=' rather than ' = '.
items.when: The query filters or groups bonds by bond_type.

items.statement: A growth rate computed as a percentage must cast the numerator to REAL (or multiply by 100.0) so that integer division does not truncate the result.
items.when: The answer is a percentage ratio of two integer-valued sums.

items.statement: When a question asks about loans belonging to clients of a given gender, the join path from loan to client must pass through disp filtered to type = 'OWNER', because a client can hold non-owner dispositions on accounts.
items.when: The question attributes loan amounts to clients by a client attribute such as gender.

items.statement: A question naming a city and a county is filtered on both the City and County columns, not on the District column.
items.when: The question specifies a city and a county as location filters.

items.statement: When a question asks for administrator e-mail addresses, the answer columns are AdmEmail1 and AdmEmail2 from the schools table, not AdmEmail3.
items.when: The question asks for valid administrator e-mail addresses of schools.

items.statement: Column names referenced in a query must match the schema exactly, including spelling of columns such as CreationDate.
items.when: The query references a column whose name is similar to but not identical to a schema column.

items.statement: A date filter on a post's creation year must reference the posts table's CreationDate column, not the users table's CreationDate column.
items.when: The question asks for posts filtered by a year and the query joins posts to users.

items.statement: Counting clients in a district-based filter uses COUNT on the client identifier rather than COUNT(*) over joined rows.
items.when: The query joins district to client and the denominator is a count of clients.

items.statement: A percentage of clients filtered by a district attribute is computed over clients joined directly to district on district_id, without joining through disp or account.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of clients whose district satisfies a condition on a district column.

items.statement: The order of selected columns follows the order in which the question requests them.
items.when: The question names a metric first and a grouping or identifier column second.

items.statement: A requested percentage that is not stored as a column must be computed from its numerator and denominator columns rather than selected from a similarly named column.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage and the table offers count and enrollment columns but no matching percentage column.

items.statement: Yes/no existence questions are answered with a 'YES'/'NO' string produced by IIF over an aggregate count, rather than a boolean EXISTS expression.
items.when: The question is phrased as a yes/no question about whether any matching row exists.

items.statement: Questions asking whether a translated version of a card exists are answered by joining cards to set_translations on setCode and checking that the translation column is non-null for the requested language.
items.when: The question asks about the existence of a card in a specific language and the schema contains a set_translations table with language and translation columns.

items.statement: A COUNT over a joined parent key without DISTINCT overcounts when the child table has multiple matching rows per parent.
